title: Beauty of Joseon Expands to 1,263 Boots Stores in Britain - Retail News Asia
text:

 Why it matters
 Goodai Global has expanded Beauty of Joseon to 1,263 Boots stores across Britain, securing dedicated displays in 100 locations. 
 The retail footprint intensifies high-street competition against established international skin care brands as British consumers adopt daily sunscreen routines. 
 Goodai Global intends to use its strong British pharmacy distribution as a launchpad for further physical retail rollouts across Europe. 
 Retail News Asia newsroom analysis
 Beauty of Joseon has expanded to 1,263 Boots stores across Britain, marking one of the largest retail footprints for a Korean beauty brand in Europe.
 Owned by Goodai Global, the label secured dedicated brand displays in 100 Boots locations, giving it the largest such presence among Korean beauty competitors at the chain.
 Scaling Shelf Space in High Street Retail
 Goodai Global first entered Boots in June 2024 before building distribution across the British retailer’s national network. Securing 1,263 locations solidifies a major physical footprint as consumer demand shifts beyond online channels into high-street stores.
 The expansion allows the brand to rank consistently among Boots’ top-selling Korean beauty labels, competing directly against established international brands for physical retail shelf space.
 Rankings and Category Demand
 The company attributed its sales momentum to changing British skin care habits, including growing acceptance of sunscreen as an everyday product rather than a summer-only purchase. Its Relief Sun: Rice sunscreen benefited from shoppers seeking sun protection that wears comfortably under makeup.
 In April, the company held the first solo pop-up by a Korean beauty brand at Boots, setting up shop inside the retailer’s store at Westfield Stratford in London. During that month, the brand ranked fifth among about 200 skin care brands sold at Boots and first among roughly 20 Korean beauty labels.
 Company data also showed it took second place in Boots’ Everyday Skin category, outperforming legacy international brands in daily skin care rankings.
 European Rollout Strategy
 Known for combining traditional ingredients with modern skin care, the Korean beauty brand has turned its physical presence at Boots into a major European anchor.
 Managing stock turnover across more than a thousand storefronts allows the company to reach shoppers who buy their daily skin care in physical pharmacies rather than through cross-border internet orders.
 “Expanding to nearly 1,300 stores and increasing dedicated displays means Beauty of Joseon has become part of European consumers’ everyday lives,” a company representative said.
 Next Moves for Western Distribution
 Following the nationwide rollout announced on Friday, Goodai Global aims to broaden the international reach of K-beauty across physical retail networks.
 The brand plans to use its British retail performance as a springboard to expand its physical distribution network across Europe.
 Advertisement Advertise with us Mobile 320×100 What this means
 Unlike Korean beauty's traditional reliance on cross-border internet orders, this high-street rollout secures immediate physical dominance. The move will succeed because British shoppers now treat sunscreen as an everyday cosmetic item. Scaling shelf space directly pressures legacy international brands in Boots Everyday Skin rankings, where the label already demonstrated strong sales. However, managing stock turnover across more than a thousand storefronts introduces substantial inventory risk. If replenishment falters, category momentum will stall. Watch whether Goodai Global expands beyond its current 100 dedicated store displays.
 Sarah Chen
 Questions & Answers
 Q. How extensive is Beauty of Joseon's rollout across Boots?
 A. The brand is stocked in 1,263 Boots branches across Britain, featuring dedicated displays in 100 locations. This rollout represents one of the largest retail footprints for a Korean beauty brand in Europe, giving it the retailer's largest dedicated presence in the category.
 Q. What is driving the brand's sales growth in the British market?
 A. Growth is being propelled by shifting British skin care habits, notably the everyday use of sunscreen rather than just during summer. Shoppers have particularly favoured the brand's Relief Sun: Rice sunscreen as a daily protective product that wears comfortably under makeup.
 Q. How well has the brand ranked against competing skin care labels at Boots?
 A. In April, the label ranked fifth among roughly 200 skin care brands and first among 20 Korean competitors at Boots. Company figures also showed it took second place in the chain's Everyday Skin category, outperforming several established international rivals.
 Q. What are parent company Goodai Global's wider European plans?
 A. Goodai Global intends to use its British retail performance as a springboard to expand physical distribution networks across Europe. This strategy aims to capture consumers who prefer purchasing everyday skin care products in high-street pharmacies rather than placing cross-border online orders.
